newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES STABLE TO SOFTER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES STABLE TO SOFTER.

text.p: Short term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted stable to softer in quiet Friday trade, dealers said.
"The market was Z$164 million in surplus (at settlement) and we expect it to continue liquid because we have Z$178 million (worth of) treasury bills maturing today," commented a dealer.

Discount houses were taking up 91-day treasury bills from the central bank at 19 percent after Thursday's weekly tender, down from last week's 19.36 percent and selling them into the market at around 18.50 percent.

NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were quoted softer at 19.50 percent from 19.75 while bankers acceptances, also at 19.50 percent across the board, were unchanged from their previous levels.
Call money shed one percentage point to 18 percent.
